title: DeviceSide test records
description: The files in docs/integrations/<integration>/test-records/: a rig record per suite (<suite>.json, the step file's name: <action>.json or <action>-<option>.json), the maintainers' manual sign-offs (_manual.json) and the facts the rig's fact cases found (_facts.json). The rules they serve are docs/evidence.md's (Sign-off format, The coverage check); scripts/check_release.py and scripts/gen_compat.py read them. A file's integration is its folder's.

integration.description: The integration's key, its bundle's folder name.

model.description: The model ID: a Zigbee device's Basic-cluster model (e.g. LWA012) on every integration, else the integration's model ID; docs/models.yaml must list it.

firmware.description: As the integration reports it; null when it reports none.

class.description: The class the call reached (IntegrationInfo.capability, as the action's result reports it); null where the integration named none, or names no classes.

record.description: A rig run of one suite. Format 2 is what the rig writes: the devices each test reached. Format 1 is a markdown record converted once (device-classes plan, step 5b), with the run's devices on the record, not per test; it credits as the markdown did and is no sign-off.

action.description: The action the suite tests: its step file's `action`.

options.description: The step file's `options`, sorted; absent when it has none.

result.description: pass when every test passed or was skipped.

commit.description: The deviceside commit the run tested.

package.description: The git tree of integrations/<integration>/ at the run's commit, which check_release compares with the release's.

devices.description: Format 1 only: the run's devices, in the order the record listed them.

record_device.description: Format 1: a device of the run, or a native group (its own entry, not its members).

name.description: The name HA's registry gave the model, where the record named one.

id.description: The case: `<test>[<role>]`, with ` observed` for a watched case.

domain.description: The domain of the entity the case targeted; absent when it targeted none.

role.description: The profile role the case targets.

result.description: not observed: a watched case nobody watched.

reason.description: Why a skipped case didn't run, e.g. none in the profile.

fact.description: A fact case (a watched case, or a firmware fact's): it runs only with --facts and its result is a row of _facts.json, so a record lists it skipped.

test_v1.description: Format 1: a test as the markdown Tests table held it.

classes.description: The markdown's Capability cell: the classes a passing test reached (a group's members', each once), empty for a dash; absent when the record had no Capability column.

test_v2.description: Format 2: a test with the devices it reached. A test that ran lists them, and its domain; a skipped one lists none and says why, unless it is a fact case.

group.description: The target was a native group: devices are its members, each with its class.

manual.description: _manual.json: a maintainer's hand tests, a row each, added in a PR. A row is a sign-off by its commit (docs/evidence.md, Release gate).

manual_row.description: Either the devices tested, each with the class it reached, and the actions that passed on all of them (a row credits each class to each action, so split a row whose actions reached different classes), or a change that sends no new call: no_call_changed.

commit.description: The commit tested: on main or a release/ branch, holding the package as the release does.

tester.description: A GitHub handle, without the @: one of the integration's maintainers or a repo maintainer.

manual_device.description: A model id (docs/models.yaml, never a household's device name) and the class it reached.

facts.description: _facts.json: what the rig's fact cases found, dated, a row each; rows are only ever added, as each is a fact that stands until evidence contradicts it.

suite.description: The suite's name (its record's file name): case ids repeat across suites.

kind.description: How the fact was seen: automated (a firmware fact's case that passed or failed) or observed (a watched case a person answered).

fact_device.description: A device the case ran on. The rig writes its class; a row converted from markdown has none, and keeps the name its record gave the model.
